## Task-1 (5-points)

Suppose you are trying to answer the following research question: Using the mtcars dataset, which car, with at least 6 cylinders, has the highest fuel efficiency (mpg)? Report the single row in the data set that answers this question.

A chat bot spits out the following code.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
mtcars |>
  filter(cyl > 6, mpg > 20) |>
  select(mpg, cyl) |>
  arrange(mpg) |>
  slice_head(n = 5)
```
:::


In your .qmd file, write the correct code in your code chunk that fixes/changes the code chunk above to answer the question.

*Fix below. A lot of unnecessary code that does not pertain to the research question. There is not reason to filter mpg > 20, and nothing in the problem tells us to select only 2 columns. slice_head() is also used incorrectly, and should be set to 1 instead of 5.*


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
mtcars |>
  filter(cyl >= 6) |>
  arrange(mpg) |>
  slice_head(n = 1)
```

Cadillac Fleetwood 10.4   8  472 205 2.93 5.25 17.98  0  0    3    4

## Task-2 (5-points)

In 2-3 sentences, explain why this code won't work and instead returns an error. Note: You do not have to fix the code, just articulate **why** this code will not run. 


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
mtcars |>
  select(mpg, cyl) |>
  filter(cyl >= 6, hp > 150) |>
  arrange(desc(hp)) |>
  slice_head(n = 5)
```
:::



*The code will not work because we are using `filter()` on a column that no longer exsists in our mtcars data set. Order matters, and we are piping a data set with only mpg and cyl into filter.*

## Task-3 (5-points)

Using the `mtcars` dataset, report how many cars have at least 4 cylinders, have a mpg above 15, and have a horsepower **per** cylinder (horsepower divided by cylinder) lower than the mean horsepower **per** cylinder across the 32 cars. Provide the appropriate code in a code-chunk that answers this question.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
mtcars |>
  mutate(hp_per_cyl = hp / cyl) |>
  filter(cyl >= 4, mpg > 15, hp_per_cyl < mean(hp_per_cyl)) |>
  select(mpg, cyl, hp, hp_per_cyl) |>
  count()
```
:::


## Task-4 (5-points)

The following code below applies a weighted moving average using weights of 0.25, 0.5, and 0.25 using the `filter` function.

For each observation, it calculates a weighted average of the observation and its two neighbors. For example, for the middle observation (6):

$0.25(4) + 0.5(6) + 0.25(8) = 6$

The result is a smoothed version of the original data. Values at the boundaries are NA because there aren't enough neighboring observations to calculate the weighted average.

The function needs to be called from the `stats` package. Type the code below into your .qmd file, and then add to the code below to make the code function as intended. Note, do **not** library the stats package to answer this question.

Reminder: If you can not get this code to work, your document will not render unless you stop the code chunk from evaluating. 

*Package masking is when two different packages share a common name. Because we `library(tidyverse)` at the top of the document, the `filter()` function comes from tidyverse, and not the stats package. We can specify a package by the package name and :: next to the function name, as seen below.*


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
stats::filter(
  c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10),
  c(0.25, 0.5, 0.25),
  sides = 2
)
```
:::
